findings.problem: RouteWorkflow has no typestate enum or explicit state machine; lifecycle is represented as free-form booleans and a status string
findings.failure_mode: any combination of fields is allowed (e.g. is_sent=true with status="pending" or is_validated=false), so illegal domain states are representable and no transition invariants are enforced
findings.fix: define a `RouteState` enum with variants (e.g. Unvalidated, Validated, Sent) and replace status + booleans + optional timestamp with a single `state: RouteState` field; mark_sent becomes `fn mark_sent(state: RouteState) -> Result<RouteState, RouteError>` enforcing valid transitions only

findings.problem: status is a public String field; callers can set any string value including invalid, inconsistent, or malformed values
findings.failure_mode: a caller can set `status = "banana"` or leave status="pending" while is_sent=true, producing undetectable state corruption at runtime with no type-level guarantee
findings.fix: replace `status: String` with an enum field (e.g. `state: RouteState`) and remove the free-form string; the type system enforces only valid values exist

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are public booleans representing lifecycle stages independently
findings.failure_mode: booleans are composable into invalid states (is_validated=true, is_sent=false, status="sent"); there is no enforced ordering or single-source-of-truth for lifecycle, so race conditions and logical bugs are undetectable at compile time
findings.fix: replace both booleans with a single `state: RouteState` enum that encodes the lifecycle as mutually exclusive variants with explicit transitions; remove is_validated and is_sent entirely

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is an Option<u64> optional lifecycle field, separate from the status string and boolean flags
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some(...) while is_sent=false or status!="sent", or None while is_sent=true — the optional field is decoupled from the lifecycle state, creating inconsistent snapshots that are silent and unguarded
findings.fix: move the timestamp into the typestate enum variant that owns it, e.g. `RouteState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`, so the timestamp only exists when the route is actually in the sent state

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain validation or newtype wrapper
findings.failure_mode: any arbitrary string (empty, whitespace, SQL-injection payload, wrong-format UUID) is accepted; no validation, no length cap, no format check — illegal IDs are silently accepted by the domain
findings.fix: define a `RouteId` newtype with a smart constructor that validates format and length, returning a typed error on invalid input; replace `id: String` with `id: RouteId`

findings.problem: raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) cross the parse boundary directly into the domain struct with no fallible smart constructor; no parsing layer exists
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct RouteWorkflow with any combination of invalid fields (e.g. empty id, status="invalid", is_sent=true, is_validated=false, sent_at_epoch_ms=None), bypassing all domain invariants at the boundary — hostile input is never parsed or validated before entering the core
findings.fix: add a `RouteWorkflowInput` DTO at the shell boundary, a fallible `RouteWorkflow::try_from(input) -> Result<Self, RouteError>` smart constructor that validates all fields, and a `RouteState` enum for lifecycle; core logic consumes only the trusted domain type

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance claim
no profiler data or allocation analysis for the hot path
no second-ring evidence tied to actual symbols/artifacts
no command-truth evidence (no verified build/test/run commands)
residual_risk: static review only — no commands run. The crate has six BLOCKER findings: raw primitives (String id, String status, bool lifecycle flags, Option<u64> timestamp) make illegal states representable with zero type-level invariants, no parse boundary at the shell/core boundary, and mark_sent has no precondition enforcement. Without a typestate enum, smart constructors, and typed error taxonomy, any caller can silently construct and transition the route into inconsistent states.
